claims.text: A 3D-printed, topologically optimized lattice architecture can reduce the effective density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The lattice architecture can reduce effective density without substantially degrading room-temperature or elevated-temperature strength.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa at 25 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a bulk density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
Thin HfMoTaTiZr lattice struts can retain a mostly solid-solution microstructure after laser powder-bed fusion and homogenization.
Precisely controlled thin struts can carry sufficient load to preserve strength capacity.
Interstitial open space within the lattice reduces the component's effective density.
A well-designed lattice topology localizes stress in robust struts.
Stress localization in robust struts maintains load-bearing capacity while unoccupied volume reduces mass.
Compositional changes intended to reduce density could degrade ductility or introduce embrittling phases.
The lattice will have at least 10–15% lower effective density than the as-cast baseline.
The lattice will retain a compressive yield strength above approximately 1400 MPa at 25 °C.
The lattice will retain a compressive yield strength above approximately 700 MPa at 1000 °C.
The open-lattice design can preserve at least 80–90% of the as-cast strengths up to 1000 °C.
Additive-manufacturing porosity or microcracking may compromise the mechanical properties of the lattice.
A 1200 °C, two-hour homogenization treatment may not fully mitigate microsegregation in the lattice struts.

contradictions.description: The rejection rule permits strengths as low as 80% of baseline (1280 MPa at 25 °C and 684 MPa at 1000 °C), even though the stated predictions require more than 1400 MPa and 700 MPa and the boundary invokes retention of 80–90%. Thus some results that fail the explicit strength predictions would not reject the hypothesis.
